results.title: Random slugs can collide and overwrite existing links

triage.reason: Concrete fix specified: POST /links must retry random slug generation until an unused slug is found instead of overwriting an existing mapping.

work.summary: Fixed POST /links to retry slug generation until an unused slug is found (src/server.ts:32-38), using the existing LinkStore.has() check, so a random collision can no longer silently overwrite an existing link. Added a test (test/basic.test.ts) that injects a slugFn returning a duplicate slug three times before a free one, and verifies the first link's redirect target is preserved.

results.title: URLs without a scheme are accepted and produce broken redirects

triage.reason: Confirmed: isValidUrl in src/url.ts strips http(s):// before validating, so scheme-less input like "example.com" passes and is stored/redirected verbatim, producing a relative Location header; javascript:/ftp:/data: are already rejected by the existing regex, narrowing the actual fix needed.

work.summary: Fixed isValidUrl in src/url.ts to parse the input with the URL constructor and require protocol http: or https:, rejecting scheme-less input (e.g. "example.com") and other schemes (javascript:, ftp:, data:) with 400. Added tests covering scheme-less and the three disallowed-scheme cases in test/basic.test.ts.

results.title: GET /stats/:slug returns 500 for an unknown slug

triage.reason: Root cause and exact fix are identified (missing not-found guard before using store.get result in the /stats/:slug route) with a concrete expected outcome (404 + {"error":"not found"}).

work.summary: Fixed GET /stats/:slug crashing with 500 on unknown slug. The handler used store.get(parts[1])! (non-null assertion) and then dereferenced .slug on undefined, throwing and hitting the catch-all 500 handler. Now it checks for a missing link and returns 404 {"error": "not found"}, matching the redirect route's behavior. Added a test verifying the 404 response for an unknown slug.

results.title: HEAD requests are counted as clicks

triage.reason: Concrete fix located: src/server.ts calls store.recordClick for both GET and HEAD; gating it to GET only resolves the issue with a clear test to add.

work.summary: Fixed HEAD requests being counted as clicks: store.recordClick is now only called when req.method === "GET", while HEAD still returns 302 with the Location header. Added a test verifying HEAD gets a 302 redirect but clicks remain 0.

triage.reason: Concrete endpoint, request field, regex validation rule, and explicit 400/409 status codes are all specified.

work.summary: Added custom slug support to POST /links: validates slug against ^[a-z0-9-]{3,32}$ (400 if invalid), checks for existing slug (409 if taken, leaving the original link untouched), and falls back to randomSlug() when no slug is provided.

triage.reason: Concrete, testable behavior (optional expiresInSeconds on create, 410+{"error":"expired"} on GET after expiry, no click counted) with clear touch points in store.ts and server.ts, though a few edge cases (invalid input error shape, stats endpoint behavior) are left to implementer judgment.

work.summary: Added optional expiresInSeconds to POST /links; GET /:slug now returns 410 {"error":"expired"} and skips click counting once a link has expired. Links without the field never expire. Invalid (non-positive-integer) expiresInSeconds is rejected with 400.

triage.reason: Concrete, testable spec (DELETE /links/:slug → 204/404, subsequent GET/stats → 404) against a small, well-understood codebase with a clear seam to extend.

work.summary: Added DELETE /links/:slug (204 if existed, 404 otherwise) backed by a new LinkStore.delete() method. Also fixed GET /stats/:slug, which previously threw (500) on a missing slug instead of returning 404 — needed so deleted/nonexistent slugs behave correctly per the issue. Added tests covering delete-then-404 for both GET /:slug and GET /stats/:slug, plus deleting a nonexistent slug.

triage.reason: Concrete response shape, params, and ordering are specified; only cursor encoding and the GET /links vs GET /:slug route-order collision are left to sane implementation defaults.

work.summary: Added GET /links endpoint with cursor-based pagination (items + nextCursor, default limit 20, max 100, cursor = last slug of previous page, 400 on unknown cursor). Added tests covering ordering, pagination, limit capping, and invalid cursor handling.

results.title: Rate limit link creation per client

triage.reason: Issue specifies a concrete, testable behavior (10 req/min/IP on POST /links, 429 with retry-after on the 11th) against a small plain-Node http server with no existing rate-limiting code, so an agent can implement and test it directly.

work.summary: Added a sliding-window RateLimiter (src/rateLimit.ts) keyed by client IP, limiting POST /links to 10 requests per minute. The 11th request in the window now returns 429 with a retry-after header (seconds). Redirects (GET /:slug) and stats (GET /stats/:slug) are untouched. Added tests verifying the 429 + retry-after behavior, window reset after waiting, and that redirects/stats remain unlimited.

issuesFound: Minor/non-blocking: RateLimiter's internal Map never evicts entries for IPs that stop sending requests, so memory grows unboundedly over the process lifetime in a long-running server. Not a correctness issue for this issue's scope, but worth a follow-up if abuse from many distinct IPs is a concern.

Test coverage gap (non-blocking): the new tests only exercise a single client IP; there's no test confirming two different client IPs are rate-limited independently. The implementation (Map keyed by IP) is correct by inspection, but the 'per client' aspect of the issue isn't directly verified by a test.
